title: The Samadhi in Lahore
hookLine: his memorial stands beside Lahore Fort, near a gurdwara

lines: A PALE BUILDING BY THE FORT.
URNS OF ASHES UNDER A CANOPY.
cards: Stand in old Lahore with your back to the great walls of the Fort. In front of you rises a pale building with a gilded dome and small domes around it, and arched windows of carved stone. Next to it is a gurdwara.
Nearby, the huge red mosque of a Mughal emperor. Inside the pale building, under a canopy, are urns of ashes. This is where the Maharaja who took Lahore came to rest.

teach.b: A samadhi, in the Punjab, is a memorial raised over the place where a person was cremated. It isn't a tomb in the usual sense: there's no body, only ashes and memory.
Ranjit Singh's samadhi was begun after his death by his son, and finished in the years of the troubles you've been hearing about.
Right beside it stands Gurdwara Dera Sahib, which marks the place where Sikh tradition says Guru Arjan, the Fifth Guru, was martyred in Lahore.
So the Maharaja's memorial stands next to the memory of a Guru who gave his life; the two buildings share one courtyard of memory.
Sikh tradition links Guru Arjan's last days in Lahore with a line from one of his own hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib: what you do seems sweet to me, and Nanak asks only for the treasure of the Name.
A king's memorial of gold and stone stands beside the memory of a Guru who asked for nothing but the Name.
And inside the samadhi, small memorials keep the queens and serving women who died on his pyre, the sorrow from five days ago, close beside him.
A memorial keeps a name in one place, so people can come and stand before it.
Sikhs from across the border still visit when they can. The building can't tell you everything about the man, but it gives the memory an address.

how: Sikh pilgrims who travel to Lahore visit Gurdwara Dera Sahib, the place of Guru Arjan's martyrdom, and the Samadhi of Maharaja Ranjit Singh beside it.

o: the place where the Maharaja was crowned.
the place where Sikh tradition says Guru Arjan was martyred.

games.why: Gurdwara Dera Sahib stands beside the samadhi, so a king's memorial and a Guru's martyrdom share one courtyard of memory.

practice: In your mind, walk to a place where someone is remembered, a grave, a plaque, a bench with a name, a photo on a shelf, and stand before it, noticing the stone or wood, the light, the name.
Let one memory come up by itself, and stay with it. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.
